title: New crazy workflow for making 3D assets
author: FearlessCounty3487
selftext: I discovered some crazy new technique for making my 3D assets. I tried to use the image to 3D or text to 3D AIs but they never create exactly what I want. I also tried AI with Blender but that was always lacking in detail. Now what I do is first generate a model from an image, import it into Godot, and then ask Claude Opus to build a new model based on that but with the improvements and details I need. For some weird reason that works perfectly every time.

comments.author: Andr92x
comments.body:
I would still give Blender a chance.

It's all about how you use it. I finally found somewhat a good workflow to build cars with alot of detail.

Text to image via ChatGPT, make Claude write the prompt, you would like to have front, back, both sides, 3/4 front and back.

Let Claude start clean in Blender and do alot of measurements. My experience is that a generated mesh from meshyAI just make it harder for Claude.

Let Claude use chatgpts images as references.

And then just iterate with Claude on what you want and what looks wrong. I'm in the middle of making the interior as detailed as possible. I gave Claude real images of hollowed out race cars to look at. It's looks like this right now but there will be more polishing later

https://preview.redd.it/vl182advqkwh1.jpeg?width=1080&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=77b48bc093b95c799ca6ae7f251e49270f57b19d

comments.author: mr_undeadpickle77
comments.body:
https://reddit.com/link/1xa3gju/video/lf99d0jchowh1/player

This worked really well, thanks!  
**Workflow:** Give claude the goal and any details > generate an image of the 3d object > use the image in meshy 3d to generate the 3d model > send model to Godot game engine > have claude recreate/optimize the model in Godot > describe any Godot animation and tweaks and claude writes the script > output to a 3d preview window/claude artifact.

Edit: used Claude Opus 5.5 on High, GPT Image 2.5 and Meshy 7

**Full prompt:**

    I want to try a workflow for making 3D assets on one smaller asset first:
    1) start with an image of the object, 2) generate a rough 3D model with Meshy/Tripo,
    3) import it into Godot, 4) have Claude build an improved replacement using that model as reference.
    
    Use this treasure chest image. Generate with the Higgsfield MCP using the newest Meshy.
    I approve 2 model generations — don't stop to ask. Loop until you achieve the goal and
    don't stop for approvals unless something is dangerous/unsafe.
    
    Then:
    - Make an interactive artifact so I can view and play with the Godot chest on my phone.
    - Bake Meshy's textures onto the rebuilt chest.
    
    Opening:
    - When tapped, add anticipation: the chest shakes and rocks side to side, the lid struggles to open, then snaps open and slightly overshoots before settling.
    - Right as the lid is thrown open, a very brief but impactful burst of energy/light.
    - Coins and gems of all sizes and colors burst out. It should practically overflow
      (double what it is now), with some spilling over the rim onto the ground.
    - Real physics: every opening is random. Some pieces roll, some spin, some settle quickly, and bigger pieces feel heavier.
    - Each gem and coin glows by a different amount, gem facets are noticeable, and there's the occasional very large gem.
    - Magic: particles swirl around the chest (the vortex only happens on opening and
      dissipates after a few seconds), the interior glows with an aura, and wide pulsing sun rays have golden particles spiraling upward before fading.
    - Add a few treasure artifacts resting in the pile inside the chest (silver goblet, ornate cross, worn parchment scrolls, etc.). They don't spill out. Make them larger.
    
    Closing:
    - Two options: leave the loot where it landed, or vacuum it back into the chest before the lid closes. The vacuum should suck in everything, including the aura and particles.
    - Vacuum anticipation: floor loot lifts slightly, hovers and trembles, dips back toward the floor, then gets siphoned in quickly.
    - Lessen the chest's shuddering during the vacuum.
    - The lid closes right as the last pieces enter, with no delay.
    - The slam should feel snappy and impactful, like a lid containing an awesome power.
      More particles get sucked in as it closes, then cut off abruptly when it slams shut.
    - One last little jump as the treasure enters, then the chest falls to the floor with a
      thud. The movement should tilt organically and feel weighty, not lift perfectly in one
      direction. The lid settles with secondary, overlapping motion.
    
    Stage:
    - Dark background with a soft radial spotlight on the chest. The spotlight gets stronger
      when tapped.
    - Controls for light amount, radius and color.
    - Objects react to the light with more twinkles, glows from certain angles and refractions where possible.
    
    Housekeeping:
    - Commit the project files when done.
    - Check performance, especially when the chest first opens.
    - Render a shareable demo video showing the chest opening and closing several times and all the features. When the animation changes, redo the video and archive the old one.
    
    Finally:
    - Write a Claude and a Codex skill that recreates this whole 3D model + animation process
      for any object. 
    - Whenever animation is involved, apply Disney's animation principles wherever they make
      sense, at about 50% strength by default: never bland or linear, but not cartoony.
